and the famous [mantra] ending with *svāhā* should be performed, concluding with *tāraka*.

One should perform one hundred thousand recitations and then offer oblations of ghee colored with that [same substance] by a tenth part; O Mahāsena, once perfected, she becomes a servant who carries out one's tasks.
She deludes the entire earth with her all-encompassing gaze, surpassing even the most excellent non-humans;
she draws away the essence of Śakra—what then need be said regarding mere mortals here on earth?
O Śāṅkarī, this knowledge of the Siddhas is indeed sufficient for householders; it is a means of invisibility and likewise a means of delusion.

Because she produces happiness, she is therefore remembered as Bhailakhī;
because she delivers one from difficulties (durga), she is considered Durgā.
The Queen of Knowledge, which originated from the mouth of Śiva, has been proclaimed by me;
it has been declared in brief and in summary, and now it is being spoken by me once again.
For the purpose of curing cough and asthma, O you who are purified by perfected knowledge,
[I worship] Varuṇa, who is indeed for the sake of the pacification of cough, beginning with the syllable Om.
With this very mantra, the wise one should cause [the disciple] to grasp water in his hand,
having carefully extracted the words "Tāraka amṛtāya."
Likewise, the second step is considered to be for the sake of the form of nectar;
you are the nectar arising from nectar, and beyond that, the supreme nectar itself.
This mantra, which bestows immortality and greatness, is a destroyer of sins.
One should drink eight *sulu* fruits in sequence, increasing the number by one each time.
After eight days, one should drink eight mouthfuls of that radiance;
O Mahāsena, this is for the cessation of cough and asthma.
This [mantra], when recited, is perfected and is considered the wish-fulfilling cow of knowledge;
O Śāṅkarī, for all cases of cough and asthma, there is no other [remedy] than this.
For [this] is indeed the state of being the *samaya* of the syllable *oṃ*.
O Varuṇa, with this [mantra], one should take water in the right hand:
"For the sake of immortality, for that which originates from immortality, for the reality of immortality, and for the majesty of immortality."
Now, therefore, I shall explain the knowledge of thieves by which it arises, as well as the practice of the mantra-leader for that purpose.
One should employ the word *raktoṣṭhī* as the first step, followed by *mātaṅgī*;
the third step is the *paiśāca* [mantra], which one should join with *bhūto bha*.
One should cause the syllable *dve* to descend; immediately after that, the syllable *ṇa*;
then another syllable, *adarśa*; and likewise, one should place *darśa* outside.
"Have the thief seized, and likewise have the western quarter sprinkled;
by means of this principal mantra, one should perform the rite of command for the maiden."
On the following day, the practitioner, having bathed, should perform the ritual action;
he should first rub his own left thumb with ignorance (ignorance-mantra).
Then, taking a lac [of the substance], one should rub the left thumb-nail;
having purified it with sesame oil, one should grind it once again.
Having turned toward the north, one should then consecrate the maiden;
one should place flowers upon her head and display the *tattva-aṅguṣṭha* mudrā to her.
O son, at the time of midday, when the sky is cloudless,
a young girl facing the east beholds everything as a wonder.
She should point out the thief, and he should describe his true nature;
this is a further elaboration, my child, as told by Śiva in the past.
Red-lipped Mātaṅgī, O Bhūtoḍbhā, descend, descend! Come, come!
Seize this thief who has been seen; here she is!
With this mantra, flowers consecrated by the mantra should be given upon the heads of the two maidens on the day of the rite.

On the second day, at the time of midday, having bathed and become pure, one facing north should rub one’s own left thumb with sour substances while reciting one’s own mantra; thereafter, one should smear it profusely with thick lac.
Having placed flowers on the heads of two virgins with this mantra, one should show the thumb;
it reveals the thief.
O Six-faced One, I shall further proclaim the perfected vidyā:
Hrīṃ Caṇḍakāpālini Dantakiṭikkiṭi Śuṣkeṣu.
Having washed rice grains with this king of mantras and recited it over them twenty-one times,
one should cause them to be given to the thieves; then the blood, crushed by their teeth, will fall from the mouths of the thieves.
In the remaining [vessels], well-ground white-colored substances fall.
Thus ends the knowledge of thieves.
Those skilled in the science of spirits (bhūta-tantra) should perform the ritual for the expulsion of spirits;
first, however, one should cause the offering of the bali-oblation to be made within the sacred precincts.
Then, after the placement of the mantra (mantranyāsa) in both forward and reverse order,
one should subsequently perform the striking (tāḍana) of the spirit for the sake of accomplishment.
Then, having released it, let it be immediately effective in bringing [the target] under control:
*Oṃ jvalanta jihva jvalanta locana kapila jaṭābhāsūra mahāsūra vidrāvaṇa trailokya ḍāmara rudra bhrama 2 ākaṭya 2 troḍa 2 moha 2 paca 2 evaṃ śuddha*.
Rudra commands: Svāhā!

If I have gone to the home, or to the heavenly world, or the world of the gods, or the world of the nāgas, or to a grove, a monastery, or a household—there I shall abide; accept the offering, accept it! I give it to you: Svāhā!
With this mantra, an offering to the Kṣetrapāla should first be presented;
afterwards, with this same mantra, the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa) and the ritual placement on the body (dehanyāsa) should be performed in both direct and reverse order.

The ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*) consists of [the fingers] from the tip of the little finger up to the tip of the thumb, ending with the thumb and the little finger. The ritual placement on the body (*dehanyāsa*) consists of [the syllables] from the head, mouth, heart, navel, and genitals down to the feet in direct order; and from the feet, genitals, navel, heart, mouth, and up to the head in reverse order.
Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner both forward and backward, one should thereafter strike the patient with white mustard seeds (*siddhārtha*).
It reveals all that has been, is being, or will be. One releases [the affliction] once the sign of proof is seen.
*Svāhā*. With this, after the hand-placement and body-placement, the striking is performed.
Thus ends the "Terrifying of Spirits."

I shall now fully describe the paralysis of speech for those who have been observed speaking auspiciously: one should write the name of the person inside that vessel using the charcoal from a *preta*.
Having fashioned a hollow from one's own excrement and cast it into a pit, one should place a stone upon it;
this will paralyze speech—what need is there to mention other [powers]?
Then, having inhaled the poison by means of the *haṃsa*-practice, one should perform exhalations while the breath is situated in the sun; that one should withdraw it—what wonder is there in that?
Now I shall further explain the measurement and the collection;
one should carefully measure the messenger's upper garment by means of an easy method.
At the end of that, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) consisting of the hand, the body, and the self;
first, one should especially place the blazing limb upon the body or the head.
For those who have not renounced their passions, for animals, and especially for men, the *jamala* birth exists; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter.
It is true, truly, there is no doubt; and [it occurs] every other year.
283a) Īśvara said:
Now listen as the procedure for the rosary (akṣasūtra) is being told: that which consists of one hundred and eight beads is proclaimed as the best.
Half of that size is praised as medium; half of that again is beneficial as small.
That which is made of Rudrākṣa beads is for great servants, granting liberation and being supremely auspicious.
The path should be constructed with one-faced, three-faced, four-faced, five-faced, or six-faced [stones]; therefore, one should avoid using those that are friendly [to the enemy].
One should place the mouth against the mouth; one should avoid placing the mouth at the base.
This indeed applies to all gems, as well as those produced from trees and water.
The *putraja* [bead] is for the sake of obtaining sons; the *padmaja* [bead] is for wealth and other such goals.
The *indrākṣa* thread bestows sovereignty, and the *śakrākṣa* thread is exactly like it.
One who desires well-being should have this leader of threads, which wards off misfortune and is free from calamity, fashioned from gold or silver; furthermore, it may be made of other metals.
One should join trapu, sīmā, and ayas for the purpose of killing, as well as mahāsaṃkha.

That [fire] is to be worshipped in the direct order (anuloma), and the Rudras in the reverse order (viloma);
one should offer oblations, either by the number seven or five, for each individual offering.
Thus the daily rite has been declared; the specific [rites] follow the previous method of increase.
For an omen occurring in the intermediate space, the expiation shall be half of that.
For terrestrial [spirits], there are one hundred oblations; for those of the throat and at the feet as well.
And in all portents, as well as in great portents, there are [specific] oblations.
For those seized by all diseases, for those whose souls are afflicted by the lords of planetary spirits,
for those seized by calamities, and for those whose souls are entangled by obstacles.
One should employ this [rite] for the pacification of those who have been tormented;
and an ablution (*abhiṣeka*) should be performed with the remnants of the oblations (*saṃpātāhuti*) consecrated by mantras.
With nine jars, one less than one hundred and twenty-one mantras should be recited daily during the consecration ceremony.
Day after day, one should perform [the rite], remember [the deity], conquer [the obstacles], and offer oblations;
that prepared sacrificial porridge (caru) should be given to one who has been consecrated.
By merely sipping that [water], one is not afflicted by any misfortune;
and the *khaṇḍarudra-śānti* has been proclaimed by the Supreme Lord.
And according to what has been declared, for each and every seat (*pīṭha*) of the Rudras and their stations (*pada*), one should recite,
offer oblations (*homa*), and present nine sacrificial portions (*avadāna*), [measuring] the height and girth of a horse's hoof.
Black sesame seeds, clarified butter, and mango leaves previously prepared as nectars.
White mustard seeds, parched grains, fragrant flowers, and leaves from milk-exuding trees should be offered as oblations; likewise, sacrificial fuel sticks and rice and other such items.
For each individual Rudra, one thousand oblations of clarified butter should be offered with care; in its absence, they should be offered with the substances as prescribed.
One should perform a thousand repetitions of each individual word;
one should avoid those who have not attained perfection and those whose conduct is improper.
Those who have resorted to the left-hand path (vāmācāra) are censured in this scripture;
moreover, those whose conduct is secretive must always be avoided.
Those who have attained the final realization, whose conduct is pure, and whose vows are firm—
even they are difficult to restrain when they possess the power to suppress and to seize.
Having first understood the purification of the Guru, one should thereafter commence the rite of pacification;
it should be performed day by day, or whenever a great portent has arisen.
These thirty-eight [deities] have been proclaimed by the gods; by them this [goddess] is worshipped, both in reverse and in direct order, by the Rudras and by Vyomaśiva.
In the eighty-one squares, one should arrange thirty-two nine-square units starting from Īśāna, comprising five hundred and four squares, increased by eight, six, and three.
Following that, according to the measurement of the street-segments (vīthikā), are the Rākṣasa, Skanda, Aryaman,
Jambhaka, Pilipicchaka, and the supreme Graha.

Outside of this [maṇḍala], following the sequence stated by Satika, in all the rows [beginning with] the eastern direction, there are likewise [the syllables] Ca-ra-kṣā and so forth; and then again, the pair Vaṃ-sa.
The eight protections should be assigned in sequence, and likewise the cities in the nine squares;
indeed, within this [grid], a single square is formed by means of nine squares.
Thus indeed has the measurement of the site been described in brief;
in this very manner, one should fashion the marks of the mandala within the mandala.
However, one should further divide it into ten thousand compartments; in that placement, a ninefold multiplication must be performed, as in the case of the site-plan for a region.
Now I shall further explain another characteristic of sacred sites (vāstu):
they may be hexagonal, triangular, circular, shaped like an axle, like a womb (yoni), octagonal, or like a half-moon.
Or rather, it should be made according to the true principle, devoid of cords and bamboo;
or one may fashion a square in the center for all [the deities].
One should lay out the lines for the Raju and Aṃśa as before;
having divided the square into three parts, one should designate the third part as the Vāstu.
Below the Brahma-pīṭha is Vṛddha; in the Saraka is Vighnamardaka; below the thread is the one called Dharmadaṇḍa; and in the temple is Cakrapāda.
The eight lines of the cord are established for all these sites;
the two beams situated at the corners are invincible and difficult to withstand.
Of the four cords, there are six parts and likewise two parts;
from the mouth, the ankle, and the forearm, there should be four parts consisting of two parts each.
In the heart, the secret place, and likewise in the belly, there should be four six-petalled [sections];
thus, nine squares are to be assigned, with three-petalled lotuses placed in sequence.
When, in the same manner, [the deity] is installed in the temple of the gods,
Brahmā is in the center on nine squares, while Marīci and the others are as before.
The deities to be invoked should be known as having two feet or one foot;
just as in the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) within a temple, so too is it beneficial in the hundred-squared grid (*śatapada*).

In that context, the planets, the *āskandas*, and so forth should be understood as having four feet; the *daras*, the *rakṣās*, and so forth have the *bhūtas* as their feet; and the *raṅgas*, the *vaṃśas*, and so forth are as previously described.
In the establishment of a country, the site-plan (vāstu) should consist of thirty-four squares;
one should arrange the eighty-one-square Brahmā-grid in the central location.
Marīci, Vivasvat, Mitra, and Pṛthivīdhara. (287b) [The text is not clear.]
And regarding the protection of the field, as before, one must again cultivate the fifth [member];
thus, one causes the factor of the field to be performed. For the purpose of preventing internal loss, they are separated.
